notes: Pinned OCI SDK contract: CreateMediaWorkflowConfiguration, GetMediaWorkflowConfiguration, ListMediaWorkflowConfigurations, UpdateMediaWorkflowConfiguration, and DeleteMediaWorkflowConfiguration are present in v65.110.0. Create, get, and update return the MediaWorkflowConfiguration body directly, while delete returns only headers and no service-local work-request identifier. MediaWorkflowConfiguration exposes lifecycle states ACTIVE and DELETED.

Pinned provider coverage is unconfirmed. formal/sources.lock still points at github.com/oracle/terraform-provider-oci@eb653febb1bab4cc6650a96d404a8baf36fdf671, but the accessible local provider inventory did not expose a checked-in MediaWorkflowConfiguration resource or data source. The providerResource and datasource names therefore stay provisional OCI-style placeholders so manifest-owned catalog promotion can happen later without blocking the runtime review.

Repo-authored runtime treats create and update as synchronous read-after-write flows. The reviewed controller-backed contract does not publish provisioning or updating lifecycle buckets and settles ACTIVE as success after a follow-up GetMediaWorkflowConfiguration reread.

Repo-authored bind-versus-create is explicit: pre-create lookup requires spec.compartmentId and a non-empty spec.displayName, scopes ListMediaWorkflowConfigurations by compartment and exact display name, and adopts only a unique exact match on compartmentId plus displayName. Duplicate matches fail instead of binding arbitrarily.

Repo-authored mutation policy is narrower than the SDK surface: only displayName, parameters, freeformTags, and definedTags reconcile in place. compartmentId remains replacement-only drift, and create-time locks remain explicit unsupported drift after creation instead of implicitly using isLockOverride or lock helper APIs.

Delete confirmation is explicit in repo-authored semantics: the runtime calls DeleteMediaWorkflowConfiguration without isLockOverride and treats either a DELETED lifecycle reread or OCI NotFound as terminal. Matching create-time locks are normalized out of steady-state parity checks by ignoring OCI-populated timeCreated metadata.
